text:
reminder

closure is a myth

one of those foolish notions that enters your head at a young age and is best squashed like a bug, asap, bc it does nothing but lead u astray + waste ur time.

1/5

expressed via dork behavior like “she dumped me, but I need closure, so I'm gonna text her until I get a reason”

brotha

u got the closure

when somebody tells u "its over," that means its over

permanently over in all possible scenarios

its hard to watch someone struggle with this reality, yet its also a position everyone has found themselves in once

there is no good outcome

if they come back in two days and say, "hey, actually, its not over"

you say: "no, it's over"

because the only other option is squid behavior and massive aura loss ("I'm so happy u kicked me to the curb, slept around, and now ur willing to take me back")

this rightfully makes them loathe you, so the 2nd "its over" is imminent

and now u are just destroying ur self-respect and dignity, chasing after someone who told u to get fucked.

don't do that, here are playbooks u can use.

2/5

dignity is less about their perception of u (they're history so who cares) and more about ur perception of yourself

u want to be automatic in the face of rejection

"u didn't get the job"
"it's over"
"u are fired, pack ur shit"

whatever lines and boundaries and principles u have, when they get crossed, all automatic

same reaction for everything

u can react in private on ur own time, but right now, u want to get to the point where its just...

"ok, see u later."

throw deuces and get the fuck out of there✌️

3/5

this will really fuck with people when u get it right -- which isnt the point of it -- but if u get dumped and can just shrug

or offer something like I've used: "well, its been real, it's been fun, it ain't been real fun."

and then boom, right out the door

they're sitting there like wtf

"did he ever care about me?"

now THEY need closure

but this is stupid petty behavior to not even think about or engage in.

u will make the mistake once, where u got in their head so bad, that they'll call u and u pick up. 

"can we talk things over?"

brief rebound, she gets closure -- "they are who we thought they were" -- and she dumps u again.

that's why when its over, its over forever.

4/5

u can always get your own self-closure

goal is, "never make the same mistake twice"

you want to figure out what parts of the mess were attributable to u.

its never 100% to 0%.

there is always some part u played in any broken relationship or job.

lets say its 50%-50%

you take that 50%, your 50%, and you take complete and total ownership of it.

you fix what is fixable, you eradicate any related defects of character so that it doesn't happen again, and then u move on.

u don't worry about the rest, that other 50%. its entirely out of ur control -- it doesn't exist.

5/5

in all these situations, u can melt down later in private

ur always gonna be shattered

there is no "just turn ur emotions off"

but I think u learn first in trading, then in life, that there are a lot of situations where there is no good outcome

there's down 20%, down 40%, and down 60%.

you take the 20% loss -- "good outcome, good process, best-case scenario" -- and move on.

this pattern is actually the sign of a very experienced trader/PM, they re-wired something, because it all goes against natural human instinct

factory install is 
1. "wait for the down 20% to rally to 0%, then exit."
2. "the good outcome is that she wants me back."

no. u are creating good outcomes and happy endings that do not exist...this is how the down 20% becomes down 60%.

is there an "upside" scenario?

that's why the goal in a lot of these, is just to escape with ur dignity intact.

u dont realize it, but u are in a bad/worse situation.

u will melt down in private over what happened

and if u handled it poorly, u will 2x melt down over "and then I made a fool of myself in front of everyone."

both are deserved. ur body is reacting as it should

the down 20% was there

u fucked around, u ate the down 60%, and u are feeling the sharp reproach of error, of shame, of cowardice, and of poor self-discipline.

the truth is that there is some upside scenario to all this

if u get blasted with horrible news, and people only see u stand up, wave goodbye and then walk out

when the dust settles, they're going to talk about how you took that shit like a G

u don't get a ton of these "true character" moments and so people always remember how it went down

"when the mask came off, he was actually tough as nails."

END 

this is why a man's final reaction in the face of death is so poignant, and inevitably becomes part of their story

Cicero "offering the neck" to his murderers, Cato pulling his guts out of his own stomach

Voltaire on his deathbed, so they say, was asked by a priest to renounce Satan...and responded with, "now is not the time for making new enemies."

this is why Montaigne writes about how many a wasted or debauched life, has ended up being redeemed by a noble death

so u may as well keep the few things they can never take from u

dignity, pride, self-respect

and "always die with dignity" is as good a name for this playbook as any.

been real, been fun

...but it ain't been real fun✌️
